chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon every truth (haqq) there is a reality (haqiqa), and upon every correct deed there is a light (nur).'

key_terms.حَقٍّ: Truth or right; that which is due or true in a divine or ontological sense.
key_terms.حَقِيقَةً: Reality or essence; the inner truth or substantive core of a matter.
key_terms.صَوَابٍ: Correctness; that which is right, accurate, or aligned with truth.
key_terms.نُوراً: Light; spiritual illumination or clarity associated with correctness.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between truth (haqq) and reality (haqiqa) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kafi’s chapter on conviction (Yaqeen), this hadith elucidates the ontological structure of truth, asserting that every 'right' (haqq) has a corresponding 'reality' (haqiqa) and every 'correctness' (sawab) is illuminated by a 'light' (nur). This teaching underscores the Shia epistemological view that divine truth is not merely propositional but possesses an inner spiritual essence and luminous guidance, essential for achieving true certainty. It reflects the Imam’s role in manifesting these realities, linking the believer’s internal conviction to the external manifestation of divine guidance.
